reason: SAM CLI is a pip-installable CLI whose README quickstart (sam init / sam build) runs locally on CPU without AWS credentials.
demo: README Get Started: Hello World app via `sam init` then `sam build`
goal: Install aws-sam-cli from the cloned repo so the `sam` command works. Then `sam init --no-interactive` with the hello-world template, Zip package type and the machine's Python runtime must create a project, and `sam build` inside it must produce .aws-sam/build with the built template and function code. No AWS credentials or Docker are available or needed.
check: The hidden test generates a Hello World app with sam init, runs sam build, and checks that the build output template and function code exist.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Oracle bug (confirms the audit): SAM CLI rejects `sam init --no-interactive --runtime ... --app-template hello-world --package-type Zip` without --dependency-manager, failing with 'Missing parameter --dependency-manager'.
v2 adds `--dependency-manager pip`, disables telemetry, and also checks that the built HelloWorldFunction/app.py contains the generated lambda_handler.
evidence: src/aws-aws-sam-cli@199c33a4 samcli/commands/init/command.py:45-49 — the non-interactive combination is [name, runtime, dependency_manager, app_template]
samcli/commands/init/command.py:119-129 — Zip package type with no location and no dependency_manager -> click.UsageError('Missing parameter --dependency-manager')
data/runs/aws-aws-sam-cli/result.json audit — with --dependency-manager pip, init+build produced .aws-sam/build/template.yaml and HelloWorldFunction/app.py
